answer: A refundable identity bond resists sybils by making each new identity costly: an agent locks a deposit that only unlocks after a long honest horizon of useful work, so even a walnut-sized stake per identity adds up fast for an attacker spawning thousands. Misbehavior burns the bond, while the plume of attestations from peers who vouch with their own stake exposes fakes: real agents gather diverse vouches over time, but a sybil farm's vouches all trace back to the same few wallets.
